title: The American Flag
subtitle: Thirteen stripes, fifty stars, and one teenager who changed the design.
description: An A1 reading and listening text on the flag of the United States: what the stripes and stars mean, how the flag changed, and the student who designed the one we see today.
source: authored for this site; no source document
passage: The American flag has three colours: red, white and blue.
It has thirteen stripes. Seven are red and six are white. The thirteen stripes are the first thirteen states.
In the corner there are fifty small white stars on blue. One star is one state. There are fifty states in the United States today.
The flag is not old in this form. The first flag with thirteen stars is from 1777. Then the country got bigger, and the flag changed many times.
When a new state arrived, the country put a new star on the flag. The stripes stayed at thirteen.
Alaska became a state in 1959. Hawaii became a state in 1959 too. So in 1960 the country needed a new flag with fifty stars.
A student from Ohio, Robert Heft, made a fifty-star design for a school project in 1958. His teacher gave him a B.
Then the government chose his design. The teacher changed the mark to an A.
Americans see this flag every day: in schools, in front of houses, at sports games. There is also a flag on the moon, from 1969.
People call the flag “the Stars and Stripes”. Now you know why.

items.prompt: How many stripes does the flag have?
items.explanation: Thirteen: seven red and six white.

items.prompt: What do the fifty stars mean?
items.explanation: One star is one state, and there are fifty states.

items.prompt: What do the thirteen stripes mean?
items.explanation: The first thirteen states — the old colonies.

items.prompt: What happened when a new state arrived?
options: The country put a new star on the flag
The country put a new stripe on the flag
items.explanation: A new star. The stripes stayed at thirteen.
Robert Heft, a student, for a school project in 1958.

items.prompt: What mark did his teacher give him at first?
items.explanation: A B. The teacher changed it to an A after the government chose the design.

exercises.title: True or False?
exercises.instructions: Decide if each sentence is true or false.

items.explanation: False — it has three: red, white and blue.
True — the country got bigger, and the flag changed many times.

items.statement: The first flag with thirteen stars is from 1777.
items.explanation: True — that is the date in the text.

items.statement: There are fifty stripes on the flag.
items.explanation: False — there are fifty stars and thirteen stripes.

items.statement: There is an American flag on the moon.

exercises.title: Words from the Text
exercises.instructions: Choose the word that matches the meaning.

items.prompt: A long line of colour is a ___.
items.explanation: A stripe. The flag has thirteen.

items.prompt: The place where two sides meet is the ___.
items.explanation: The corner. The stars are in the corner.

items.prompt: The plan or shape of something is the ___.
items.explanation: The design. Robert Heft made the fifty-star design.

items.prompt: The group of people who run a country is the ___.
A letter for your work at school, like A or B, is a ___.
items.explanation: A mark. His first mark was a B.
